channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Can traditional Chinese exercises help people with musculoskeletal disorders? - BJSM blog - social media's leading SEM voice
item.description: An umbrella review of 92 meta-analyses (1,744 trials) found high-certainty evidence that Traditional Chinese Exercises (TCEs) improved physical function and mental health in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia. Tai Chi reduced chronic MSD-related pain and stiffness and increased bone mineral density in osteopenia/osteoporosis.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of 35 trials (n = 3808 patients) found that short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effects on pain (SMD = -0.937, low certainty), function (SMD = -0.590, low certainty), and quality of life (SMD = 0.663, low certainty) in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Immediate task-specific and delayed generalized adaptations to variable dual-task training in community-dwelling older adults: a randomized waitlist-controlled trial
item.description: A randomized waitlist-controlled trial (n=50) found that 12 weeks of variable dual-task training led to immediate improvements in functional lower-limb strength (SMD = 0.54) in older adults, sustained at 3-month follow-up. Delayed improvements in functional mobility, inhibitory control, and short-term memory emerged at follow-up.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 RCTs (N=1,096) found that exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = -1.22, 95% CI [-1.72, -0.72]) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]) at ≤4 weeks after total knee arthroplasty, although the certainty of evidence was low and heterogeneity high (I²=93%).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 103 trials (5,251 participants) comparing various robot-assisted training (RAT) approaches for post-stroke upper-limb recovery found that rTMS plus RAT yielded the largest improvement on the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) with a mean difference of 9.56 points (95% CI, 7.18-11.93) compared to usual care, followed by LFES plus RAT (MD 7.52 points).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Female Team-Sport Athletes’ Physical Fitness and Jump Performance Kinematics After Plyometric Jump Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 31 articles (n=609) found that plyometric jump training (PJT) significantly improved countermovement jump height (ES = 0.550, p < 0.001), drop jump reactive strength index (ES = 0.926, p = 0.001), linear sprint speed, and agility sprint speed in adult female team-sport athletes, with longer interventions (≥ 8 weeks) showing greater benefits.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Effect of Incorporating Perceptual Learning Into Plantar Hardness Discrimination on the Risk of Falling and Muscle Torque in Patients With Hemiplegia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34) found that incorporating perceptual learning into plantar hardness discrimination significantly lowered fall risk (ES=1.48), increased knee extensors torque (ES=1.19), and improved FIM scores (ES=1.56) in stroke patients with hemiplegia.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of different physical therapies for axillary web syndrome after breast cancer surgery: A network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (1007 patients) found that soft tissue manual therapy + therapeutic exercise + low-level laser therapy significantly reduced pain (SMD = -4.40, 95% CrI: -5.52 to -3.28) and improved shoulder ROM in axillary web syndrome, while MLD + therapeutic exercise showed the largest improvement in upper-limb disability (MD = -19.01, 95% CrI: -22.52 to -15.52).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of Manual Physiotherapy Techniques for Improving Cervical Range of Motion in Infants With Congenital Muscular Torticollis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of five RCTs (n=143 infants) found a statistically significant pooled effect (Cohen's d = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.54 to 1.27, p < 0.001) in favor of manual physiotherapy techniques for improving cervical ROM in infants with congenital muscular torticollis, indicating a large overall effect.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: In a controlled laboratory study of 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR), athletes with ACL reconstruction (ACLR) showed slower response times, lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09), and persistent alterations in cortical oscillatory mechanisms related to cognitive control, motor preparation, and attentional allocation during decision-making under uncertainty.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society consensus statement, derived from a modified Delphi process with 17 expert clinicians, achieved over 80% agreement on 54 statements across three domains for managing athletic hamstring injuries, emphasizing standardized terminology, individualized criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading, and objective assessment for return-to-sport decisions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of sleep manipulation on athletic performance, cognitive function, and recovery: a systematic review of experimental studies
item.description: A systematic review of 15 experimental studies found that sleep extension generally led to enhanced athletic performance (e.g., +9.5 m in shuttle run, -0.7 s in sprint time, ~3% improvement in endurance), cognitive function, and recovery. Sleep restriction had adverse effects, while daytime napping showed mixed, context-dependent results.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Adding blood flow restriction to low-load resistance training for sarcopenia and cognitive function in oldest-old adults: an exploratory randomized controlled trial
item.description: An exploratory RCT (n=36) found that supervised low-load BFR-RT improved handgrip strength (P=0.012), 4-m walk time (P=0.044), verbal learning (P=0.003), and delayed recall (P=0.002) in oldest-old adults with sarcopenia and MCI compared to no exercise. Evidence for additional benefits of BFR over matched low-load RT was limited.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that chair-based exercise training combined with breathing exercises significantly improved functional exercise capacity (mean 6MWD difference: 50.9 m; 95% CI 2.09-99.76; p=0.042), dyspnea, and quality of life in hospitalized patients with acute exacerbations of COPD.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies suggests that neurocognitive factors, including dual-task interference, visual attention, reaction time, and cognitive fatigue, are significant contributors to ACL injury and that integrating neurocognitive challenges into rehabilitation and RTS testing may help identify athletes at risk for secondary injury.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Sex-Equitable Machine Learning Prediction of Ankle Reinjury in Individuals with Chronic Ankle Instability: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study with Fairness Audit
item.description: A 2-year prospective cohort study developed and internally validated sex-equitable machine learning models to predict ankle reinjury in 96 individuals with chronic ankle instability. The Elastic Net model achieved an AUC of 0.807, and applying sex-specific decision thresholds reduced the equalized-odds gap by 57% (to 0.164).
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Treatment Planning in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine: A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 9 studies found that large language models (LLMs) showed promising capabilities in supporting rehabilitation treatment planning, with concordance with expert opinion varying but reaching 98.75% after expert review in some cases. However, included studies reported hallucinations, underscoring the necessity of supervision.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of the effects of modified razor curl and nordic hamstring exercises on hamstring muscle strength and posterior-chain endurance in male football players
item.description: A 6-week RCT (n=45 male football players) found that both modified razor curl and Nordic hamstring exercise protocols significantly improved eccentric hamstring strength and trunk-hip extensor endurance (all p < 0.001) compared to a control group, with no significant difference in bilateral strength. MRCE may represent a practical alternative to NHE.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Post-Platelet Rich Plasma Rehabilitation Approach on Pain and Function in Subacromial Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=54) found that adding a structured post-PRP rehabilitation approach to conventional physiotherapy significantly improved pain (VAS reduced from 9.00 to 2.92 vs 9.11 to 7.96, p < 0.001) and function in subacromial pain syndrome patients over 21 days, compared to conventional physiotherapy alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: First-Hand Experience and the Value of Telerehabilitation for Chronic Knee Pain: A Discrete Choice Experiment Nested in a Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A discrete choice experiment (n=319) in Australia found that patients with firsthand experience of telerehabilitation for chronic knee pain were willing to pay AU$87.49 more for telerehabilitation consultations than those who experienced in-person care, with 68% of telerehabilitation arm participants preferring it.
item.author: PubMed
